subject: chemistry
question_text: The empirical formula of a compound is CH₂O and its molecular weight is 90. Calculate the molecular formula of the compound.

verification.note: Chapter 5 (Stoichiometry) is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.66-72), which prints the question, its star rank and a model answer. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Finding n

lines.text: n = molecular weight / empirical formula weight

steps.why: The molecular formula is a whole-number multiple of the empirical formula. Dividing the molecular weight by the empirical formula weight gives that multiple n.
common_mistakes: Using 12 + 1 + 16 = 29 for CH₂O. There are TWO hydrogen atoms: 12 + 2 + 16 = 30.
Inverting the ratio and writing n = 30 / 90.
steps.memory_tip: n asks how many empirical units fit inside one molecule: big weight divided by small weight.
steps.margin_note: The empirical formula weight 30 with its sum shown earns this mark.

steps.label: The molecular formula
steps.why: Multiplying every subscript of CH₂O by n = 3 gives the molecular formula. A check: C₃H₆O₃ weighs 36 + 6 + 48 = 90, which matches the given molecular weight.
common_mistakes: Writing (CH₂O)₃ and stopping. Expand it to C₃H₆O₃.
Multiplying only the carbon subscript by 3.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply every subscript by n, then confirm the formula weighs 90.
steps.margin_note: Box C₃H₆O₃. The weight check 36 + 6 + 48 = 90 is a free safety line.

insider_note: A three-star staple. The examiner looks for the empirical formula weight 30 computed on the page — the answer C₃H₆O₃ with no visible n = 90/30 loses the first mark.
